# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map

  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.

  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).

  main's file). With

  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE

  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.

  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS

- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:

  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);

  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,

  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  mix's `ExportWriter`, then writes each stem from a fresh build on the export's key read
  through only its composition tracks (`BuiltComposition.selectingAudio`) into an

  the write from the same float decode, normalised or not, through

  cut, later buffers read and dropped, a short read padded with silence at
  the master's depth; the measurement feeds the same count. The alpha movie rows' frames (`prores_4444`,

  straightened, and `hevc` is pinned to Main; `hevc_10bit` maps to `.hevc`
  too, is told apart by its codec name (`isMain10`), is pinned to Main 10

  `ExportWriter` FILLS the frame when a fit would leave at most

    97	    /// How the chroma key reads this layer in an HLG project (spec §11 HD-19
    98	    /// (c)): a track by its frame's SDR-project step-0 choice and its media's
    99	    /// peak (a built-in Camera Log `.log`, HD-20 (a)), a still by its own arm
   100	    /// (its cached texture's) and its `input.peak` (HD-20 (b)), every other
   101	    /// layer — text, shapes, graphics, the slate — by HD-13 (h)'s un-lift. A
   102	    /// gain-map still reads the un-lift too, as its SDR label does (HD-22 (g)).
   103	    func keyReading(

   105	        instruction: RecipeInstruction?

   118	            return KeyReading.of(rendered?.conversion, peak: layer.input?.peak)
   119	        default:
   120	            return .unlift
   121	        }
   122	    }

   124	    /// Wraps a pixel buffer as a texture through the `CVMetalTextureCache` —
   125	    /// zero-copy, because both sides are the same IOSurface — in the Metal
   126	    /// format of the buffer's own pixel format; nil for one with none.
   127	    func texture(from buffer: CVPixelBuffer, live: inout [CVMetalTexture]) -> MTLTexture? {

   129	        let height = CVPixelBufferGetHeight(buffer)
   130	        guard width > 0, height > 0,

content.content:
(core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

none that starts there has progressed — keyed keys at their end values,
  unkeyed ones at what is held. The playhead no longer decides where an
  edit lands, so fields do not move with it. Selecting an action parks the
  playhead at its end (one frame short when the action ends with the clip,
  whose end tick composes nothing), so the preview shows the state the
  fields show.
- **CI-3 — Pan, mono, compressor, noise reduction, duck and keep-pitch go
  to the BASE props whatever is selected.** The app routes them there
  (`InspectorBinding.structural(audio:for:)`, beside

# Spec §11 — decisions: Screen recording (road map 3)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

- **Screen recording is IN; camera recording and callouts stay OUT** (road
  map 3, reversing §1's day-one non-goal). A screen recording is the input
  the whole product was shaped around; camera capture is a second capture
  stack and callouts are a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant.
  What ScreenCaptureKit draws into the pixels for free — the cursor, and
  a ring around each click — is taken; nothing is reconstructed afterwards.
  **Amended by CAM-1** (camera recording, CR0): camera recording is now IN
  — a camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and
  track, through this recorder's panel (`camera-recording.md`); callouts
  stay OUT.
- **A recording is ordinary media.** The recorder writes a file and the app
  imports it through exactly the path File ▸ Open and Add Media… use
  (`adoptImported`, the two-try placement). The model learns nothing: no
  source kind, no flag, no schema bump. Every op, cache and export treats a
  recording clip as the media clip it is.
- **The file lives in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`**, named by date and
  time, never in the package and never in the temporary directory: an
  untitled document has no package (§5.6), and a recording is ORIGINAL
  footage, so the one place it may not go is where a cache is regenerable.
  Consolidate carries it in on the same terms as any other file.
  `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides the folder for a proof.
  **Amended by NM-4** (rename R0): `~/Movies/Reelcut Recordings/` is now
  `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`.
- **The canvas takes the recorder's RATE; the media record takes the
  file's.** ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when the screen changes,
  so its files are variable-rate and the probe honestly reports something
  like 24981/1000 (measured); the untitled document is built at the 30 or
  60 the panel asked for, because that is the grid the person chose, and
  `set_canvas` is NOT used for it afterwards — an untitled document's
  first project is not an undo step, and the rate is part of what the
  document IS.
- **The panel asks for the grants; the tool never does.** `Transcriber`'s
  rule for two grants: Screen Recording (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`
  reads, `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` asks) and Microphone
  (`AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus`, `requestAccess`). The microphone
  status is read BEFORE any `AVCaptureDeviceInput` is constructed, because
  that initializer prompts on its own. `record_screen` reads and refuses by
  name with the fix in the sentence. The built app needs BOTH the plist
  usage key and the hardened-runtime entitlement
  `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` for the microphone; Screen
  Recording needs neither.
- **A press of Record asks for Screen Recording once, and every later
  press opens System Settings at the pane** (2026-09-28). The first press
  without the grant calls `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess`, and the panel
  remembers it across launches in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`, because
  the system prompt appears once per app, not once per launch; every later
  press opens `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture`
  through `NSWorkspace` and the note says System Settings is open at that
  pane (the plain refusal when `open` answers false). The flag counts only
  in a launchd-owned launch (`getppid() == 1`, `launchClause` empty): a
  shell-launched press always asks and never writes it, because TCC gives
  that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1), and a flag written there would stop
  a later Finder launch from ever being put in the pane's list. A
  `.denied` or `.restricted` microphone opens `Privacy_Microphone` the same
  way; `.notDetermined` still asks, and a prompt's answer never opens
  a second panel) for what is one row. With Microphone Only chosen, System
  Audio, Show Clicks and Size grey out with their values kept, so the panel
  does not jump (hiding them would resize the panel under the pointer);
  Rate stays live, because it is a new project's rate; Record with
  Microphone "Off" refuses with a note; and the Screen Recording permission
  is neither checked nor asked for. The row persists for the session only,
  as a picked window does. **The countdown and the status item are
  unchanged**: the same 3-2-1 with the live meter, the same coral dot,
  elapsed time and Pause/Resume/Stop menu — no microphone glyph in the menu
  bar, since the dot already means "capturing" and a glyph is a third width
  to size the item for. **The panel STAYS UP during a voice-over** (the
  owner's choice), with its live microphone meter, since nothing is filmed:
  this amends the panel decision above, which now holds for every source
  except Microphone Only. While a voice-over records, the panel keeps its
  rows locked as for any recording, its meter live, its footnote the coral
  dot (the pause glyph while paused) and the elapsed time, Record reading
  Stop and a Pause/Resume button beside it. Close takes the panel away and
  the recording carries on under the status item: the welcome button and
  the quit guard show the panel again, and File ▸ Stop Recording (⌥⌘N,
  retitled while any recording runs, `AppDelegate.swift`'s
  `validateMenuItem`) and the status item stop the voice-over, as
  `AppDelegate+Recording.swift`'s `newRecording` routes by the panel's
  phase. **The files** are
  `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a`, one file
  per stretch between pauses, as a screen recording's are — never the
  capture output's own pause into one file, which is unmeasured here and
  would give Pause a second machine. **Landing in an open project**: every
  file on ONE new back track named "Microphone", touching, from the
  playhead, in one undo step "Add Recording" — where a screen recording's
  microphone lands today — never the picture rule (the front track), and
  never an existing Microphone track, since no rule says which track is
  "the" voice track. **As a new project**: the first file is the document
  (1920×1080 at the chosen rate), and later files touch it on its one
  track. **MCP**: `record_screen` gains `source`, `"screen"` (the default)
  or `"voice_over"`; with a voice-over the default microphone is implied,
  and `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`,
  `include_framejob_windows` (added when the Include Frame Job windows decision
  below met this one) and `microphone: false` are refused by name, and only the Microphone
  permission is read. The tool's refusal order is `seconds`, then `source`
  (its value, then the screen-only arguments given — a JSON null is not
  given — then `microphone: false`), then the existing argument checks,
  the Microphone grant and `project`; for a voice-over nothing comes after
  (no Screen Recording grant, no lookup). Not a new `record_voice_over` tool, which would
  change the tool count, the catalog order a probe reads, the assistant's
  withheld list and parity for one tool. **A microphone that stops on its
  own ends the voice-over** — nothing else is recording — and what it wrote
  lands, the note saying so. Whether it stopped on its own is judged by
  when its report ARRIVED: a did-finish stamped before the segment's
  `stoppedAt` is still "on its own" when a Pause or Stop press reached the
  main thread first, and it ends the voice-over from paused as from
  recording. **The result shape**: a voice-over ends as an

AU-68 and AU-69 are AP6's third part (Enhance the microphone when a recording lands; survey B8),
recorded before its code.

- **AU-68 — A follow-up, not part of the landing.** The landing commits at once and is unchanged:
  `RecordingLanding`, `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, the step names, the notes, the panel's
  note and reveal, and `record_screen`'s fields. Enhance Voice (AU-60…AU-65, unchanged) follows as
  its OWN undo step, "Enhance Voice", once the voice's caches exist.
  (a) **The voice clips** are every clip in the open container whose media path is one of the
  recording's voice paths: each segment's `micDescriptor`, each `unreadable[].micDescriptor`, and
  for a voice-over each segment's `descriptor` (`RecordingEnhance.voicePaths`). Never the
  picture's, the camera's or the system audio's; none without a microphone.
  (b) **Readiness.** Each voice clip's media has a current loudness cache
  (`MediaImporter.loudnessIsCurrent`), and `media.speech`, or a current speech cache
  (`speechIsCurrent`), or `SileroVAD.isAvailable` false — Enhance then skips the clip in its own
  sentence.
  (c) **Busy** is any of: `document.isLiveEditing`; `document.scope` other than the landing's;
  and at the panel only, no editor window or a sheet already on it.
  (d) **`decide`**, in this order: no voice clip still present → `.drop` (quietly at the panel);
  analysed and not busy → `.enhance`; 300 s since the landing (`waitLimit`) → `.giveUp`;
  otherwise `.wait`.
  (e) **The panel** runs a repeating 0.5 s timer (`RecorderPanelController.landingRetryInterval`)
  in the run loop's DEFAULT mode, the landing's retry trick, so it pauses during a drag. On any
  step but `.wait` the timer is invalidated and the landing's pending entry removed FIRST, then
  the step acts, so nothing the sheet does (Cancel, no outcome, a stale answer) can leave a timer
  that puts it back up. `.enhance` runs `AudioMeasureDoor.enhanceLanded`: the press's own
  `measure` under the Measuring Sound sheet at `NormalizeChoice.targetLUFS`, committed with
  `performGroupedEdit` (a timer is not an AppKit event) as "Enhance Voice"; Cancel changes
  nothing. Nothing to enhance, a stale answer and `.giveUp` are a refusal of `enhance_voice` at
  the inspector's foot (`projectDocumentDidRefuse`); nothing beeps and the panel's note is not
  touched. `.giveUp`'s sentence: "Enhance Voice did not run on the recording: its microphone was
  not ready to measure within 5 minutes. Select its clip and choose Clip ▸ Enhance Voice."
  (f) **The tool** (`record_screen {enhance: true}`) polls `decide` through `onMain` every 0.5 s
  on the server thread, then runs `enhance_voice`'s own body at −16 LUFS
  (`AudioNormalize.defaultTargetLUFS`; a tool reads no `UserDefaults`). The answer gains
  `enhance`, the `enhance_voice` answer object, or `enhance_error`, a string: any refusal of that
  body, "No microphone clip landed on the timeline, so there was nothing to enhance." for
  `.drop`, and `.giveUp`'s sentence ending "Call enhance_voice with its clips." for `.giveUp`.
  The top-level `project` is read again after the enhance.
  (g) **Undo.** Edit ▸ Undo reads "Undo Enhance Voice", then for a document landing "Undo Add
  Recording"; for a new project it then reads the remainder's step (Add Microphone, Add
  Camera…, Add Recording Segments), or nothing when the first file is the document.
  (h) **Why.** The loudness and speech caches, and isolation's render, cannot exist before the
  media is in a project. Holding the landing for them would hold the files' landing, the note and
  the answer behind analysis that can fail; a separate step lets ⌘Z take the processing off and
  keep the recording.
- **AU-69 — The setting, the argument and the proof.** (a) A checkbox, "Enhance the microphone
  when it lands", on a row with no label directly under Microphone; enabled only while the panel
  is idle with a microphone chosen (any source), greyed otherwise with its value kept; its tooltip
  names AU-68's step. `RecordingChoice.enhanceMicrophone` is true only when it is ticked and a
  microphone is chosen. (b) Its key, `FrameJobRecordingEnhanceMicrophone`, is the panel's
  eleventh: written on change, restored on show, absent reading off; the harness and `screens.py`
  pin it. (c) **Default off**: Enhance writes eight settings, renders isolation and puts up a
  sheet, so a recording lands as recorded unless asked; the tool's default matches. (d)
  `record_screen` gains `enhance` (boolean, default false), read after `place` and before the
  Microphone grant, so both of its refusals are among the caller's own mistakes: "enhance: true
  enhances the microphone's clip, so it needs microphone: true (or source voice_over)." and then
  "enhance: true needs place: true — with place: false the microphone lands as media with no clip
  to enhance."; a non-boolean is `boolArg`'s sentence. (e) **The dev tool `land_recording`**
  (Debug and Release only) hands fixture files to the product's own code after `onFinish` — the
  panel's `recordingEnded` or the tool's landing — because the recorder needs the Microphone grant
  and a voice at the microphone, while a proof's instance records room tone under the terminal's
  grants. (f) The proof is `audio_ap6c_probe.py` (P1–P5, mutants M1–M9) and `audio_ap6c_proof.py`
  (V1–V8, over MCP, `land_recording` and exports); how a real voice-over on the RØDE sounds is
  manual check REC-19.

AU-70…AU-78 are AP7's (live loudness and true-peak metering; survey A8), recorded before its

- **AU-70 — The meter reads the TRUE mix, rebuilt from the taps off the audio thread.** Each tap,
  after its chain, copies its block (pre-envelope) and first frame
  (`round(time.value·rate/time.timescale)`; a buffer whose time is not numeric, the player's
  silent pre-roll, is skipped) into its sink's `MixRing`, a single-producer ring that takes no
  lock and allocates nothing. The consumer runs on the meter's existing 30 Hz main-thread timer
  (no new `DispatchQueue` seam): it drains every ring, sums by frame index each track ×
  `MediaPeaks.envelope(ramps, at: frame·600000/rate)` — a mono track at unity in both channels, a
  track's first two channels only — and feeds the stereo sum to a `LoudnessMeter` at the taps'
  rate. Frame f is summed once every track has delivered past it, except a track not sounding at
  f (f's tick outside every one of its own `sounding` spans — a gap between clips as well as past
  the last span; #65: the tap delivers nothing there) or more than `stallLag` (0.5 s) behind the
  leading track; such a track is silence at f and is not waited on, and a frame it does deliver
  after the sum has passed it is dropped. Frames a track delivers are summed as delivered. When
  no track sounds at the reached frame the sum fills silence up to what has been delivered, and
  with nothing delivered past it, it waits; that fill is never a `jump`, so a gap on one track or
  on every track neither holds the sum up nor resets it, and a seek across a stretch where

  not move I). Tracks reporting different rates are not measured. AVFoundation's ≤ 25 ms slew at

  tutorial from S-ST1, each cut to a state the owner would publish: once in the build current

  gave up, with the tool and the reason; each step that took noticeably longer than it should;
  which bet would have changed it. The verdict is recorded under this entry as GR-1's was
  ("**Verdict (owner, date):** …"). Each finding becomes a phase, an amendment or an issue,
  never only a note in a reply. Risk accepted: the trial may reorder the road map's phases.
- **CJ-6 — The build arrangement.** An integration worktree outside the repo
  (`~/devel/framejob-creator-jobs`, branch `creator-jobs`, from main). Each phase is one litecode
  pipeline (design → adversary → implement → review → fix), built in a lane of its own, gated
  (`make gate`) and committed there, then rebased onto the integration branch one at a time by
  one serialized integrator and gated again. At most three lanes. A lane whose next phase needs
  another lane's unlanded phase waits; it never builds against an unlanded one. Format versions
  are provisional from 38: when another lane landed a bump first, the integrator renumbers the

  split by size is `XXna`, `XXnb`, sharing its block. Phase XXn's decisions are XX-n0…XX-n9

  before its run (CAM-2's precedent). Manual checks are `JOB-n`, numbered by the integrator at

  third-party Audio Unit hosting); R5-1 (effects are closed vocabularies); `recording.md`'s
  "nothing is reconstructed afterwards" and "a recording is ordinary media"; CAM-10 (the
  recorded camera lands in the bottom-right corner); the owner's "not wanted" verdicts (GR-20,
  GR-27…GR-30). Each of those entries gains a one-line "**Noted by CJ-1** (2026-11-01): the
  non-goal it cites is lifted; this decision stands as design." so a reader of the entry is not
  misled. Risk accepted: the spec no longer says what Frame Job will not be, so a request that
  once met a non-goal now meets a road map's scope.
- **CJ-2 — Road map "creator-jobs" builds the survey's six bets in one road map, led by people
  who record themselves talking.** First TX, CU and CO (talking-head and screen tutorials), then
  VR and FC (repurposing to shorts), then SW (video podcasts), in the lanes of "Phases" below.
  The survey is `designs/creator-survey.md`; its next tier and "Not worth chasing" table are not
  in this road map and are neither in nor out. Survey decisions 5, 8 and 10 are asked at the
  phase that needs them.
- **CJ-3 — The key rule: a feature that needs a language model or a cloud model works only when
  the person's key for it is present; without it, its menu items and controls are disabled with
  a tooltip naming the key and where it is set, and its tools refuse in that sentence (owner,
  2026-11-01).** The keys are the Anthropic key (AI-8, Settings ▸ Assistant) and the AssemblyAI
  key (R6-5, Settings ▸ Transcription). There is no on-device fallback: Apple FoundationModels
  is not used, and filler detection stays AssemblyAI's (TR-7 stands). Not "significant AI", and
  never gated: on-device Apple frameworks and the models Frame Job already bundles — Vision, Sound
  Analysis, Speech (`SpeechEngine`), Silero VAD and `AUSoundIsolation`. "Present" is a stored,
  non-empty key or the proof's environment variable, in R6-5's order; whether the key is VALID
  is the service's answer to a request and never decides a control. A result already made with a
  key stays usable without one: R6-16 and R6-21 stand, so a gate disables only what would make
  a new request. AI-1 stands: a Claude call is the helper's. One implementation (CJ1's
  `ModelKeys`), applied to the shipped features (Remove Filler Words, Generate Captions'
  AssemblyAI engine, `transcribe`'s cloud engine, `transcribe_for_fillers`, the Assistant) as
  well as the bets'. Risk accepted: a person with no keys sees greyed commands where they once
  saw a sheet that explained itself; the tooltip carries the explanation instead.
- **CJ-4 — The recorder may ask for Input Monitoring, opt-in (owner, 2026-11-01; amends
  `recording.md`'s first bullet).** Only the recorder panel asks, and only when the person turns
  on a capture that needs it (CU's shortcut capture). The tool never asks: `record_screen` reads
  the grant and refuses by name with the fix, as it does for Screen Recording and Microphone
  (`recording.md`'s grant rule). Nothing asks at launch, and nothing else listens to the
  keyboard. No global hotkey is added; `RecorderStatusItem`'s reason for having none stands. What
  is captured (modifier shortcuts by default, never secure input, a visible sign while capture is
  on) is CU's to decide. Risk accepted: a third TCC grant that an ad-hoc signed build loses at
  every `make app`, so a proof can only skip its granted tier by name and the rest is a manual
  check.
  composed over 10 s of a 1080p timeline while each runs, against idle. **Rules:** width 2 only
  if two jobs reach ≥ 1.5× one job's throughput AND `play_preview` composes ≥ 95 % of its idle
  count; the converted path only for converting media, unless it is within 10 % of the direct
  reader, when it is used for all.

| Phase | Lane | What a person gets | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| CJ0 | serial, first | The scope lifted, the record opened, the tolls paid, CJ-S1 and CJ-S2 run | — |

| CJ2a | C | `get_media_analysis` with `shots`; the analysis lane and store | CJ0 |
| CJ2b | C | Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes; the Analyzing sheet | CJ2a |
| CJ3 | C | Face tracks for agents and for VR and SW | CJ2a, CJ-S2 |

**Lane plan (at most three lanes, after CJ0).** The lanes are split by the files they touch.

- **Lane A, words:** CJ1 → TX's phases → FC's phases. CJ1 changes the filler and caption sheets
  TX builds beside; FC needs TX's sentence spans and CJ1's Anthropic gate. TX's restore phase waits
  for CJ4 (lane C) and its bulk-cut phase for CJ6 or CJ-9's verdict; FC's Make Short phase waits

- **Lane C, shared and picture:** CJ4 → CJ6 → CJ2a → CJ2b → CJ3 → CJ5 → VR's phases → SW's

1	import Foundation
     2	
     3	/// The open-time repairs of a project's media, after `project.json` is read
     4	/// and before the document is shown: the re-anchor of consolidated media
     5	/// (`ProjectDocument.reanchoringConsolidatedMedia`) and, here, the re-copy
     6	/// of a WebM or Matroska copy that is gone (spec §11 #228-O, O13 and Q3).
     7	///
     8	/// Neither is an edit. Both run where `readPackage` runs — on
     9	/// NSDocumentController's read queue for a person's File ▸ Open, on the
    10	/// lane's thread inside `withoutAsking` for an agent's `open_project` (spec
    11	/// §11 #231), on the main thread for a read AppKit runs there — before the
    12	/// document exists as far as AppKit is concerned, so they register no undo
    13	/// step, dirty nothing and show no alert; whatever save comes next writes
    14	/// the new paths out.
    15	extension ProjectDocument {
    16	
    17	    /// `readPackage`'s repairs, in order: the re-anchor first, so a
    18	    /// consolidated copy found in the package's `media/` is never copied
    19	    /// again, then the re-copy.
    20	    static func repairingMedia(_ project: ReelProject, package: URL) -> ReelProject {
    21	        let anchored = reanchoringConsolidatedMedia(project, package: package)
    22	        return recopyingMissingCopies(anchored)
    23	    }
    24	
    25	    /// Copies again every WebM or Matroska copy that is gone, from its
    26	    /// original, and points the media at the new copy with its probe.
    27	    ///
    28	    /// A media is copied again when all four hold: its copy is gone —
    29	    /// `mediaURL(for:)` resolves nothing, or resolves inside the Trash
    30	    /// (`trashed`), where Finder's delete moves the copy and its bookmark
    31	    /// follows it; it has an `original`; the original resolves; and the
    32	    /// original is still a Matroska file. The copy is the built-in one only
    33	    /// (`MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy`): never ffmpeg, never a question.
    34	    /// The Trash counts as gone HERE only; every other reader of
    35	    /// `mediaURL(for:)` still plays a copy from the Trash.
    36	    ///
    37	    /// Each copy shows #228-P's window after 1 s through `watch`, except on
    38	    /// the main thread, where a window could not be shown, and inside
    39	    /// `withoutAsking`, an agent's `open_project` (MC-5, #231): no watch is
    40	    /// passed there. Copies run one at a time (`ContainerRewrap.assist`'s
    41	    /// lock). A Cancel or any failure skips that media (Q3): a missing copy
    42	    /// stays missing, with the slate, the badge and Relink…, and the next
    43	    /// open tries again; a copy in the Trash keeps its path and bookmark.
    44	    ///
    45	    /// `trashed` is the probe's seam, so the Trash case is proved without
    46	    /// touching the real Trash; the app passes none.
    47	    static func recopyingMissingCopies(
    48	        _ project: ReelProject, watch: RewrapWatch? = RewrapProgressWindowController.watch,
    49	        trashed: (URL) -> Bool = isTrashed
    50	    ) -> ReelProject {
    51	        let shown = Thread.isMainThread || MediaImporter.isWithoutAsking ? nil : watch
    52	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
    53	        for media in project.snapshot.media where media.original != nil {
    54	            let copy = mediaURL(for: media)
    55	            guard copy == nil || copy.map(trashed) == true else { continue }
    56	            guard let source = originalURL(for: media), ContainerRewrap.isMatroska(source) else {
    57	                continue
    58	            }
    59	            guard let descriptor = try? MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy(of: source, watch: shown)
    60	            else { continue }
    61	            ops.append(
    62	                .relinkMedia(
    63	                    media: media.id, path: descriptor.path, bookmark: descriptor.bookmark,
    64	                    probe: descriptor))
    65	        }
    66	        guard !ops.isEmpty else { return project }
    67	        // Only `.applied` is a repair; both other arms leave it as opened.
    68	        return (try? project.applying(ops)).project ?? project
    69	    }
    70	}

- **CAM-9 — A camera beside the screen (CR3a), recorded before its code.** `ScreenRecorder.start`
  with a display, window or picked source and `choice.camera` set also records the camera: one
  `(Camera).mov` per segment beside the screen's movie, paused and resumed with it, each placed
  against the screen by E2 (CAM-2's second estimator). The result carries the camera's files and
  offsets. CAM-3's files, codec and warm-up, CAM-5 (5)'s take and CAM-7 (7)'s adopt rule stand.
  1. **The start.** The order is `.busy`, the source guards, Screen Recording, then the Camera
     grant (read, never asked). Then the camera lookup ("No camera with the id … is
     connected.", `.cameraDevice`) and its format (`chosenFormat`, CAM-6 (3)). Then the
     Microphone grant and device, the folder, the recording output, the `.screen` frame watch
     (a throw is `.startFailed`) and the microphone capture. The camera is taken LAST
     (`takeCameraCapture(…, adopting: mayAsk)`, CAM-5 (5), CAM-7 (7)); a throw there stops an
     adopted microphone session and refuses. Without a camera `start` is as before: no `.screen`
     output, the same order.
  2. **The warm-up comes before the stream.** The state is `.arming` while the capture starts or
     joins its prepared start. On its answer ONE main turn runs `launchScreen`: the microphone
     file's `startRecording` (when a microphone was chosen), then `stream.startCapture`, then
     segment 0's camera writer is armed (CR0: the order of the starts made no measurable
     difference). Without a camera `start` calls `launchScreen` in its own turn, so road map 3
     R0 q6b's order is kept. A camera that fails to start, or stops on its own while arming,
     fails the start with its `.cameraDevice` sentence. The arm ceiling covers the warm-up.
     `camera.note` is the warm-up's note.
  3. **E2.** The watch is on the stream only with a camera, built with two frame intervals at
     the recording's rate as its bound (`2 / rate` seconds: 33.3 ms at 60 fps; CR0's E2 fell
     9–22 ms after E1). It keeps the PTS (seconds, as delivered; CR0 measured them on the host
     clock) of every COMPLETE frame for 2 s. Each segment's did-start is stamped on the host
     clock where it arrives (E1). E2 is the first kept or later complete frame at or after E1
     and no more than the bound after it. A segment's question is dropped at its close (a pause,
     the finishing), so a frame of a later segment never answers it. No frame in that window, or
     none by the close, leaves E2 unset.
  4. **The offset** is the camera's first buffer's PTS (host clock) minus E2, else minus E1, in
