objections.evidence: app/Sources/Compositor+Sources.swift:38–63 (the .track arm the pass hooks into). The CU-S4 rule bounds only parse ≤ 300 ms and state ≤ 20 µs 'once precomputed'. chrome-inspector-keys.md CI-3: 'the core's door is unchanged and set_action_end still takes them from an agent'. core/src/actions.rs:9–17: numbers interpolate generically. K6 measures capture CPU only.
objections.fix: Add a GPU-time and memory row for the cursor pass at 1080p, 4K and 5K Best, with a bound fixed before the run, in the style of CU-S5. Consider drawing the sprite without copying the whole frame. Load and precompute cursor tracks ahead of time (at Playback.update or RecipeSource.set, off main), and say what a frame does when the track is not ready yet, with the export waiting as it does for ramps. Bound the precompute time for the one-hour fixture in CU-S4/T2. Make `smoothing` and `hide_idle` base-only in the CORE (the recipe reads the base value, or set_action_end refuses them), not only through the inspector's routing.

objections.where: CU1 'image sampler' with CU-S1 A5 rule vs K6
objections.claim: The image rule allows NSCursor.currentSystem plus a TIFF hash at up to 1 ms median per call. The sampler runs alongside the 120 Hz position poll and its rate is never stated. At 120 Hz that is about 12 % of a core, four times K6's 3 % bound.
objections.evidence: cu.md:366–368 (≤ 1 ms median), cu.md:530–532 (120 Hz sampler; image sampler 'deduplicated by image bytes', rate unspecified), cu.md:565–566 (K6 ≤ 3 % of one core).
objections.fix: Fix the image sampler's rate in CU-11, for example ≤ 10 Hz plus on each click, or tie A5's per-call bound to K6 (rate × cost ≤ 1 % of a core). State it in CU1.

objections.where: CU-S2 instrument; CU1 K1/K2; CU3a L1; CU3b B1
objections.claim: Every timing and mapping measurement is taken with the cursor burned in (showsCursor = true). The shipped default, Separate, records with showsCursor false and under 420v instead of BGRA. ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when the screen changes, and with the cursor out of the picture a moving pointer no longer dirties the screen. Frame delivery, E2's availability (no complete frame within the bound means E1, at 21 ms) and the movie's first frame can all differ, so the anchor verdict may not hold for Separate recordings, and nothing re-measures it.
objections.evidence: recording.md: 'ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when the screen changes'. CAM-9 (3)/(4): a still screen leaves E2 unset and E1 is used. cu.md:380 (the instrument records with showsCursor = true); L1 attaches a file to an In-the-picture recording; B1 checks only that no cursor pixels remain.
objections.fix: Add a CU-S2 row, and a CU3b proof row, recorded with Separate's exact configuration. Use a truth that does not depend on the burned pointer, such as an instrument window moved in step with the warped cursor, or a flat field that changes colour at each posted click. Fix the bound before the run, and state E2-versus-E1 use on a still screen.

objections.where: CU1, CU3b, CU6 acceptance, proof rows and mutants
objections.claim: The acceptance and most mutants of CU1, CU3b and CU6 live only in granted tiers: Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, and Accessibility for the poster. An ad-hoc-signed Release build loses those grants at every `make app`, so the pipeline will skip these rows by name and the mutants will never be killed by a script.
objections.evidence: cj.md CJ-4: 'a third TCC grant that an ad-hoc signed build loses at every make app, so a proof can only skip its granted tier by name'. CU1's mutants (E1 anchor, watch left off, watch not removed, geometry once, read-back skipped, buffer not reset) and CU6's 'secure-input check removed' are killed only by K1–K5 and Y3/Y4.
objections.fix: Give each of these phases an ungranted, scriptable tier. Factor the decisions into pure, probe-callable values, for example: a CursorCaptureBuffer that takes synthetic samples and segments; a key filter `accept(event, secure:, mode:)`; and the watch-attach rule as a function of the choice. Drive them through swift_build.py probes, so every listed mutant has a scripted killer. Keep the granted rows as extra coverage, and turn their residue into JOB rows.

objections.where: CU-34 / CU3a MediaImporter+Cursor ('its movie size equals the file's'); CU-2 header 'movie size'
objections.claim: The size check will silently drop the cursor for window recordings of odd size. The header's movie size comes from the stream's configured size, while the encoder rounds an odd dimension up to even. The sizes will not match, so the file is never attached and a Separate recording shows no pointer.
objections.evidence: AgentCatalog+Recording.swift, record_screen 'size': 'An odd dimension is rounded up to even by the encoder.' RecordingSetup.swift:217–220: stream.width and height come from the point size × factor, rounded, and can be odd.
objections.fix: Write the header's movie size from the written file (read back at segment close) or as the encoder's even-rounded size, and define CU-S2's pixels-per-point against it. Make CU-34 tolerate the encoder's +1 padding. Add a K or L row with an odd-sized window.

objections.where: Phases CU0, CU3a, CU9 (and CU1)

objections.where: CU8 timing ('An overlay under 0.4 s merges with the next'); O2
